title: ChatGPT secretly put up a wall for writing style: no longer imitate the writing style of living authors

content_html:
Recently, OpenAI quietly added a new restriction to ChatGPT's rules: it will no longer fully replicate the unique writing styles of living authors. This adjustment was not publicly announced but was silently included in the functional rules, with a clear purpose: to further narrow the space for copyright issues.

Testing has shown that this barrier has already been established. When users ask ChatGPT to imitate the opening of a story based on a living author, adapt classic texts, or create content using their writing style, ChatGPT will directly refuse to fully replicate the author's specific style and language rhythm. For example, if asked to write an opening in Stephen King's style, rewrite "The Odyssey" in the style of that horror master, or start writing in the tone of Amy Tan, the system will no longer respond. What it is willing to do is to refer to general creative elements such as themes, narrative logic, and atmosphere building to produce truly original content.

Interestingly, this barrier only applies to the living. When it comes to authors like Charles Dickens, Ernest Hemingway, and William Shakespeare, who have long passed away, users can still request imitations and style replication, and ChatGPT will respond and write as usual.

The legal rationale behind this is not complicated. Current U.S. copyright laws protect only the specific textual expressions created by authors and do not establish copyright barriers around abstract writing styles. Industry experts believe that OpenAI introduced this restriction mainly to actively reduce potential copyright disputes and lower the operational risks for the company — it is a defensive compliance test in the field of literary creation copyright within the AI industry.

As generative AI becomes increasingly capable of speaking and writing like a particular person, the copyright ownership of replicating creators' styles and secondary creation based on existing works has long been a focal point for the global AI industry and the literary world. Relevant industry standards and legal details are still being gradually improved, and this new wall built by ChatGPT is just another brick quietly laid in this ongoing struggle.

content_html_zh:
最近，OpenAI悄悄给ChatGPT的规则添加了新的限制：它将不再完全复制在世作者的独特写作风格。 这一调整并未公开宣布，而是默默地纳入了功能规则中，目的很明确：进一步缩小版权问题的空间。

测试表明这个屏障已经建立。 当用户要求ChatGPT模仿在世作家的故事开头、改编经典文本或利用他们的写作风格创作内容时，ChatGPT将直接拒绝完全复制作者的特定风格和语言节奏。 例如，如果要求以斯蒂芬·金的风格写一个开头，以那位恐怖大师的风格重写《奥德赛》，或者以谭恩美的语气开始写作，系统将不再响应。 它愿意做的，是参考主题、叙事逻辑、氛围营造等一般创作元素，制作出真正的原创内容。

有趣的是，这个障碍只适用于活着的人。 当谈到查尔斯·狄更斯、欧内斯特·海明威和威廉·莎士比亚等早已去世的作家时，用户仍然可以请求模仿和风格复制，ChatGPT 会照常回复和写作。

这背后的法律依据并不复杂。 现行的美国版权法仅保护作者创作的特定文本表达，并不围绕抽象写作风格设置版权障碍。 业内专家认为，OpenAI出台这一限制措施，主要是为了积极减少潜在的版权纠纷，降低公司的运营风险，是AI行业在文学创作版权领域的一次防御性合规考验。

随着生成式人工智能越来越能够像特定的人一样说话和写作，复制创作者风格并在现有作品的基础上进行二次创作的版权归属长期以来一直是全球人工智能产业和文学界关注的焦点。 相关行业标准和法律细节仍在逐步完善中，而ChatGPT筑起的这堵新墙，只是这场持续斗争中悄然铺设的又一块砖。
